external_sentence: On CPTAC-3 (337 patients, same GDC pipeline; PMID 32649874, 34358469) the model reaches AUROC 0.994 and accuracy 95.5%; in its 131 Asian patients, AUROC 1.000 (TCGA has only 17 Asian patients in this cohort). On Uppsala RNA seq (175 patients; GEO record GSE81089 says a pathologist reviewed the histology again in 2013) it reaches AUROC 0.988, but accuracy only 90.9%: the ranking transfers while the 0.5 cut point drifts on a new pipeline. The nine gene pair rules, which compare genes inside one sample, do not drift: accuracy 98.3% there and 87.3% to 97.3% on four microarray cohorts (France, Sweden, Canada and the SBV IMPROVER set; PMID 23698379, 23032747, 24305008, 23966112). Of 87 Korean adenocarcinomas (GSE40419, PMID 22975805), 96.6% were called LUAD, including 100% of 36 never smokers.
top20_checks: All 20 also differ strongly in a plain t test (q < 1e-10). On their own, they separate the subtypes in CPTAC-3 too (single gene AUROC 0.849 to 0.982).
top10_notes:
- **1. KRT5, higher in LUSC.** Keratin 5 is a structural protein of the basal cells of skin and other layered epithelia (PMID 20030639). Yes, for LUSC. CK5/6 is one of the four standard stains used to subtype lung cancer biopsies (PMID 25120805), and KRT5 with AGR2 separates LUSC from LUAD (PMID 34150027).
- **2. S100A7, higher in LUSC.** S100A7 (psoriasin) is a calcium binding protein made by skin cells that also draws in immune cells (PMID 9693957). Yes, for LUSC. It was reported as a biomarker of lung squamous carcinoma (PMID 25745359).
- **3. KRT6A, higher in LUSC.** Keratin 6A is a stress keratin that layered epithelia switch on after injury (PMID 10866680). Yes, for LUSC. It was reported as a marker that separates LUSC from LUAD (PMID 29069744).
- **4. ELFN2, higher in LUAD.** ELFN2 is a cell surface protein that pairs with glutamate receptors at nerve synapses (PMID 33790745). Unclear. Its LUAD pattern is strong here and holds in CPTAC-3, but I found no lung subtyping study.
- **5. KRT6B, higher in LUSC.** Keratin 6B is the close partner of keratin 6A in layered, stressed epithelia (PMID 10866680). Yes, for LUSC; reported among genes that separate LUSC from LUAD (PMID 29069744).
- **6. DSC3, higher in LUSC.** Desmocollin 3 is the desmosome partner of desmoglein 3 in squamous epithelium (PMID 19287461). Yes, for LUSC. It marks squamous differentiation (PMID 19287461), and a meta analysis lists it among stains for lung squamous carcinoma (PMID 35126682).
- **7. CLCA2, higher in LUSC.** CLCA2 is a chloride channel helper protein of layered epithelia (PMID 25548429). Yes, for LUSC. It was proposed as a stain that separates squamous from adenocarcinoma (PMID 25548429).
- **8. DSG3, higher in LUSC.** Desmoglein 3 is a desmosome protein that glues squamous cells together; it is the target of the autoantibodies in pemphigus (PMID 28492232). Yes, for LUSC. It is a sensitive and specific stain for lung squamous carcinoma (PMID 19342368) and was confirmed by staining tumours (PMID 26380766).
- **9. BCL2L15, higher in LUAD.** BCL2L15 (Bfk) is a weak cell death protein of the BCL2 family (PMID 12700646). Unclear. A PubMed search found no study of BCL2L15 in lung cancer subtyping; its strong, replicated LUAD pattern makes it a new lead, not an established marker.
- **10. BNC1, higher in LUSC.** Basonuclin 1 is a zinc finger protein of the growing basal cells of layered epithelia such as skin and oesophagus (PMID 9727087). Likely, for LUSC, as a basal cell gene; I found no study that tests it as a lung stain.
top2_sentence: The top two genes, KRT5 and S100A7, are both higher in LUSC, so I would add the top LUAD gene, ELFN2, to give each type a positive stain. KRT5 is already stained in practice as part of CK5/6 (PMID 25120805), so it doubles as a check that the method works.
label_noise_sentence: Partly: "LUAD" tumours called LUSC carry LUSC changes more often than the tumours the model agrees with (odds ratio 4.3, p = 0.039); for "LUSC" tumours called LUAD the trend is the same but not significant (odds ratio 2.0, p = 0.15).
short_label_sentence: Some of its rare mistakes may be label problems: tumours labelled LUAD but called LUSC carry LUSC DNA changes more often than expected.
